### T-064 — Wood theme items deferred during the design-match pass

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · open_

Four things were deliberately left undone in the wood-theme design-match work, none of them
requested and all chosen for scope. The Habitat grid stays `repeat(4, 1fr)` sized by its container,
so its column pitch (165.6 CSS px in `editor--wood`) is wider than the reference's ~122 px; that is
a card-width difference (reference cards ≈532 px, the story's ≈578 to 662), not a styling one, so do
not "fix" it by switching to content-sized columns without re-measuring. `.blong-inspector__body`
keeps a `max-height` plus scroll (raised to 420px with a thin warm scrollbar) although the reference
shows no scroll container at all, because removing it would let very large JSON dumps push the plate
arbitrarily tall. The inspector's wood margin is `0.7rem/0.8rem` (≈11.2 px) against the reference's
≈11 px, which is fine, but if the plate padding is ever changed, `:last-child`'s `flex: 1` makes the
change invisible except in that margin. Finally, row/table hover and `p-highlight` colours are
interpolated from the design's static pixels, because the reference has no hover state to measure.

### T-069 — PrimeReact's theme cascade resets structural geometry; wood is patched

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · open_

`primereact/resources/primereact.min.css` is now an explicitly empty stub ("has been deprecated …
included in the build as an empty file") and the real structural CSS is injected by each component
inside `@layer primereact`, while `themeRegistry` injects `theme.css` separately. Some of those
theme rules use shorthands that reset geometry the structural sheet set — the ActionHint caret
(`.p-overlaypanel:before { border: solid transparent }` wiping `border-width: 10px`) is the one
found so far.

Only the wood variant is worked around, by restating
`.blong-theme-wood .p-overlaypanel::before/::after` unlayered with `!important`. The glass variant
and every stock PrimeReact theme still render a nub instead of a caret. The proper fix is either to
inject `theme.css` into `@layer primereact` before the structural sheet, or to raise the structural
layer's priority — worth doing centrally rather than per variant. Audit other components for the
same pattern, meaning any theme rule that sets a `border`, `margin` or `padding` shorthand over a
structural rule: `p-overlaypanel::before/after` is the only caret in this app today, but Tooltip,
ConfirmPopup and others may have equivalents.

### T-098 — Pivot dropdown lists load every option; add paging/search for large record sets

> _2026-09-16 · core/blong-browser · open_

A pivot materialises all dropdown options as rows and the dropdowns are unpaged, so an ACL list over
a large record universe (persons, invoices) is unusable - which is why the design puts scopes in the
pivot and per-record exceptions on a searchable page. A searchable, server-paged multi-select (or a
paged dropdown) would let the pivot itself handle long lists.

The diagram renderer was its only use, and it now reads the palette from the theme system instead
(D-238). The hook is still exported from the package root with its own tests, so it is a public

### T-118 — The theme context value is a fresh object on every render

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-browser · open_

Theme builds `contextValue` inline, so `useTheme()` hands out a new object per render - the same
identity landmine as F-212, where an object in an effect dependency list re-ran the effect forever.
No consumer is caught by it today (ThemeSwitcher reads primitives and stable callbacks, and the test
probe reads primitives), so this is recorded rather than fixed. A memoised value needs care because
`config` and `option` are rebuilt per render too.

### T-119 — A page taller than its tab is still clipped by the shell

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-browser · open_

The panel that hosts a page is bounded (flex-grow with min-height: 0) but does not scroll, and
.blong-app clips at overflow: hidden, so a page whose content does not bound itself is unreachable
below the fold - the flow page was, and the digest page still is (its list of digest blocks
overflows today). Bounding each page (D-243) is the fix the diagram needed; a page nobody bounds
stays broken. The shell-level fix (overflow: auto on .p-tabview-panel) was reverted because it makes
page captures run-dependent (F-222), so it needs the captures anchored to something stable first.

### T-120 — The diagram framing has no committed test

> _2026-09-21 · core/blong-browser · open_

`captureDiagram` now frames the whole drawing before capturing (D-248) — it grows the viewport until
the element is inside its scrolling box and the window — but the committed tests only ever exercise
the path where the diagram already fits, so the loop can be deleted without a test noticing.

Reproducing the path it was written for needs a page whose diagram box is shorter than the drawing:
the gateway spec's own panel can be pinned
(`[data-testid="flow-executions"]{flex:0 0 700px !important}`) which produced exactly the CI
geometry by hand (element top 551.359375, bottom 906.36 against a box ending at 900, captured
1600x356 before the fix and matching the baseline after it).

Two ways, both undecided: a spec in `realm/blong-gateway` that pins the list and asserts the capture
is unchanged (a second baseline that duplicates `observed-flow-gateway.png`), or a test of the
failure path — pinning the list tall enough that no window can frame the diagram and asserting the
`does not fit` error — which needs no baseline at all. The second is cheaper and covers the part a
reader is least able to check by eye.

### T-145 — The screenshot tolerance hides drift that is small but meaningful

> _2026-09-24 · core/blong-browser · open_

expect.toHaveScreenshot is configured with maxDiffPixelRatio 0.01 in src/playwright/config.ts: 14400
pixels on a 1600x900 shot. A whole menu group is 772 pixels, so sixteen commander baselines stayed
stale through the change that added the flow realm to the portal and nothing failed - the drift only
appeared when a capture also shifted by 2 pixels or more, which is what redis-keys and k8s-pods did.
The ratio was generous on purpose (cross-machine antialiasing, F-224), so the fix is a policy rather
than a smaller number: an absolute cap (maxDiffPixels of a few hundred) alongside the ratio, a
per-suite override where small areas matter, or a stricter comparison in the suite that owns the
chrome. Whichever is chosen, the baseline set was swept with the tolerance at zero and is accurate
now; leaving the ratio at 1% means the next such change can hide the same way.

### T-164 — Portal.tableRowClick cannot match a real table cell id

> _2026-09-27 · core/blong-browser · open_

Portal.tableRowClick(fieldName, rowIndex) in core/blong-browser/src/playwright.ts builds its locator
as getByTestId(`${fieldName}-${rowIndex}`), but a table cell's id is built by TableWidget as
`${tableId}-${rowIndex}-${field}` (TableWidget.tsx, cellId in the body renderer). No spec calls the
method, so nothing fails; it is a stale public API that would fail for the first caller. Fix by
taking the field as well — the table id and the row index are not enough to identify a cell — and
cover it with a test that clicks a known cell of a browse table, or delete the method and let
callers use getByTestId directly. The docs and the blong-playwright skill were corrected to state
the real id shape rather than the method.

### T-332 — The shared screenshot budget can hide a wrong baseline

> _2026-10-12 · core/blong-browser · open_

The default in `defineBlongConfig` is `toHaveScreenshot: {maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01}`, a share of the
image rather than a size, and on a 1600x900 viewport that is about fourteen thousand pixels.
Measured on the deployment page: the difference between a baseline showing an error dialog over an
empty table and the healthy page listing a ready Deployment is 12316 pixels, 0.86 percent — inside
the budget, so the suite stayed green for a day against a baseline anyone would call wrong (F-507,
and the realm workaround is D-534). Every suite that relies on the default, including the realm own
`blong-dev playwright` runs, can be blind in the same way, and the budget is what makes it invisible
rather than the miss. Next: consider a noise-sized default (`maxDiffPixels`) with redaction as the
documented answer for content that legitimately moves, or at least a warning when a comparison
passes with a diff close to the allowance, since that is exactly the state a stale baseline
produces.

### T-437 — A five second table wait flakes under parallel load

> _2026-10-26 · core/blong-browser · open_

waitForTableData bounds its row wait by BLONG_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT, five seconds. With four Playwright
workers on a loaded machine the edit sport category test timed out on the browse table once and
passed when re-run alone. Raising the budget would slow every spec that legitimately has nothing to
show; consider a separate, longer timeout for the data wait, or making the guard distinguish "still
loading" from "never rendered" so the failure names the real cause instead of a bare locator
timeout.

### T-438 — The harvest records record names as label keys

> _2026-10-26 · core/blong-browser · open_

The first working harvest run added 85 empty keys and about a dozen of them are not labels: test
record names (ENT-PLAY-SP-01 Sport and its siblings), a page title composed from a record name
(Browser Athlete followed by a timestamp), and document titles a spec created (European Championship
Protocol, Olympic Quota Confirmation 2024, Coach Certification Register Extract). They arrive
because useTranslate records whatever string it is handed, so a component that passes a record name
into it makes data look like a label. Find those call sites (Deck tab titles, card headers, anything
title-shaped) and give them a way to render a value without translating or recording it, then re-run
the harvest and commit only the genuine gaps such as Observe, Test runs, Sign out and the Browse
page titles. The seed was restored rather than committed with the leaks.

### T-406 — Edit a table cell without switching the row to edit mode

> _2026-10-25 · core/blong-browser · done_

ut-prime carries an `inlineEdit` mode where a cell edits in place and commits on change, with the
row keyed by the column index rather than by the row key — no pencil column and no row-edit state.
Our table edits through PrimeReact row editing, whose copy is what `onRowEditComplete` merges, so an
inline mode needs its own commit path: write the value straight into the form array like the cycle
cell does, and keep the dropdown label and `lookup` writes with it. Decide whether a cell opts in
per column or the table does.

InlineCellEditor renders the editor as the cell in a table declaring widget.inlineEdit; the commit
writes the value, its label and its lookup fields into the form array, and the cell holds the typed
text until the commit returns. Covered by two widget tests and the InlineEdit story.

### T-490 — The submission picture is cropped to what matters

> _2026-10-29 · core/blong-browser · done_

viewport, and a refused or unavailable capture leaves the fractions as the whole viewport.
